prompt:
You are a blind code reader in an empirical software-engineering study. Work only from the files in the current directory.

1. Read protocol.md first.
2. Read batch.md. It names 20 Java files by id, their path in their repository, and their local copy under files/.
3. For every file: read the whole file (use Read with offset and limit for files over 2000 lines, do not skip the tail). Identify the method with the highest cognitive complexity (the one with the most and deepest nested branches, loops and boolean chains) and name it. Then answer Q1, Q2, Q3 and Q4 from the protocol as true or false, each with one sentence of evidence from the file, and write a one-line note of the form "methodName: what it does". Do NOT derive or state the category; the mapping is applied later.
4. Blindness: do not try to read anything outside the current directory and do not try to find out anything about these classes beyond the file itself.
5. Answer with one entry per id of the batch, all 20 of them, in the required JSON form.

readings.note: remapBanListAddress: expands a ban address into its IPv4/IPv6, NAT64 and prefix-block equivalents according to remapping settings

evidence.q1: getGroupedAdaptationSetIndices merges adaptation sets into groups using trick-play and adaptation-set-switching descriptors and returns sorted int[][] groups (lines 560-634).
evidence.q2: The class is the DASH MediaPeriod: it builds track groups from the manifest period and manages selection, seeking and loading of its sample streams.
evidence.q3: AdaptationSet, Descriptor and Representation are parsed-manifest data holders read with single field accesses (adaptationSet.essentialProperties, descriptor.value).
evidence.q4: The complexity is two nested merge loops with lookups, not a switch over kinds.

readings.note: getGroupedAdaptationSetIndices: groups adaptation sets that are trick-play pairs or marked safe for switching into merged index arrays

evidence.q1: queryTablePage switches the datasource, clears the cache, then filters and sorts ServiceProxy.metadata().tables() with lambdas before paging via CollUtil.page (lines 113-141).
evidence.q2: The class is the code-generator table service: querying DDL, columns and tables for a datasource and importing/syncing table metadata into GenTable records.
evidence.q3: The objects it copies between (PigCodeGenDefaultProperties, Table, Column, GenTable, GenTableColumnEntity) are configuration and entity data holders, so by the convention this is not foreign behaviour.
evidence.q4: The branching is a filter predicate and a comparator with nested null ternaries, not a case chain.

readings.note: queryTablePage: lists the datasource's tables filtered by name/comment, sorted by update/create time, and pages them manually

evidence.q1: objectDiff reflects over the old object's fields, finds matching new fields, decides per field whether to diff, compares values and assembles a DiffDTO and formatted message string (lines 53-171).
evidence.q2: The class implements the _DIFF log-record function: a generic field-by-field diff of two objects with configurable formatting.
evidence.q3: It reads arbitrary objects' fields via reflection as a generic utility, not behaviour that belongs to any particular referenced class.
evidence.q4: The complexity is a loop with several guard conditions and a second assembly loop, not a switch over kinds.

readings.note: objectDiff: reflective field-by-field diff of two annotated objects producing DiffDTO entries and a templated change message

evidence.q1: execute splits the argument into prefix and local name, resolves the namespace, and returns an XBoolean from the function-table or extension-provider lookup (lines 48-92).
evidence.q2: The class implements one XPath function, ExtFunctionAvailable.
evidence.q3: Apart from one chain xctxt.getNamespaceContext().getNamespaceForPrefix(prefix), it works on its own argument string and function table.
evidence.q4: The branching is a namespace split and an XSL-vs-extension decision, two cases with try/catch, not a table over many kinds.

readings.note: execute: evaluates function-available(name) by parsing the QName and consulting the XSL function table or the extensions provider

evidence.q1: buildDeclareTransition converts annotation strings via converters, searches existing transitions, then drives the FSM builder chain (from/to/on/when/perform) and instantiates conditions by reflection, deciding which builder calls to make (lines 337-411).
evidence.q2: The class is the state machine builder: it defines states and transitions programmatically or from annotations, installs convention-named extension methods and instantiates state machines from the definition.
evidence.q3: It mutates its own states map through MutableState/MutableTransition APIs; getter chains such as transition.getTargetState().getStateId() are incidental.
evidence.q4: The branching mixes preconditions, an existing-transition search loop, a transition-type choice and condition instantiation; no short-case table dominates.

readings.note: buildDeclareTransition: turns a @Transit annotation into a transition, adding an action to a matching existing transition or building a new internal/local/external one with condition

evidence.q1: getTablesBydruid delegates parsing to SQLUtils.parseStatements, picks a SchemaStatVisitor by dbType, calls stmt.accept(visitor) and copies visitor.getTables() names into a list (lines 191-217).
evidence.q2: The class is a Druid filter that logs the executable SQL with parameters and execution time after statement close.
evidence.q3: It reads statement proxy data (statement.getConnectionProxy().getDirectDataSource().getDbType()) only to log it; that is the filter's purpose rather than displaced behaviour.
evidence.q4: Most of the method's complexity is the if/else-if chain on dbType choosing SQLServer, Oracle, PG or generic visitor, each case one constructor call.

readings.note: getTablesBydruid: parses SQL and extracts referenced table names using a dialect-specific Druid schema visitor

evidence.q1: isLoggable maps a java.util.logging Level onto the matching logger.isXxxEnabled() call through a nested ternary chain (lines 85-94); no value is computed from own state.
evidence.q2: The class adapts Hazelcast's ILogger to SLF4J.
evidence.q3: It only forwards to the wrapped org.slf4j.Logger; no getter chains or copying.
evidence.q4: isLoggable, getLevel and both log methods are each one chain over the Level enum with a single logger call per case.

readings.note: isLoggable: nested ternary chain translating a JUL Level into the corresponding SLF4J isXxxEnabled check
